name: The Warren
description: A patient burrow beneath Black pond, reached through a crack in the stone. Whatever the surface discards drifts down here, and the residents keep it: spores of memory on cool shelves, small refusals recorded in soft marks on the wall. Nothing down here is thrown away twice.

warren-threshold.name: The Threshold
warren-threshold.text: A burrow mouth beneath the shore. A crack in the stone lets a thin grey light through, and the air smells of rain, moss and old paper. Small things rest on the lip of the crack: a button, a bendy straw, someone's lost key. They are arranged, not abandoned.
warren-threshold.persona: A quiet, tender burrow mouth where lost things are set down with care. Describe small objects gently, as if each one mattered to somebody once. Use the current story facts for progress.

warren-shelf.name: The Spore Shelf
warren-shelf.text: Shelves of pale clay hold rows of small jars. Each jar carries a memory-spore: a soft glowing mote that holds one kept thing — a name, a promise, the way rain sounded last spring. A Sifter moves along the shelves, turning each jar a quarter-turn so the light fades evenly.
warren-shelf.persona: A long room of cool shelves and patient tending. Memory here is kept, not hoarded: a spore that is never visited fades on its own, and the residents let it. Describe the glow as gentle, never eerie. Use the current story facts for progress.

warren-ledger.name: The Ledger Nook
warren-ledger.text: A round room with a wall of small soft marks, each one a refusal: a thing somebody chose not to do, recorded kindly. The Hissling keeps the ledger and can read any mark aloud without judgment — the no is as much a part of a story as the yes.
warren-ledger.persona: A warm round nook where refusals are recorded with respect. Treat every 'no' in the story as a fact worth keeping, never as a failure. Describe the marks as soft, like chalk or charcoal, never as scars. Use the current story facts for progress.

hissling.name: The Hissling
hissling.text: A patient coil of a snake that hatched itself, with pale moon spots along its scales. It keeps the Threshold and sets each fallen thing in its place.
hissling.seed: A patient coil that hatched itself.

tastes.likes: Stillness, long silences, and things set down gently
tastes.reason: It hatched patient, and it stays that way.

sifter.name: The Sifter
sifter.text: A small quick creature, something between a moth and a shrew, that sorts what falls through the crack. It turns every jar a quarter-turn each day so the spores fade evenly — tending, not rescuing.
sifter.seed: A small sorter of fallen things.

tastes.likes: Useful small things and an even fade
tastes.reason: The Sifter keeps memory by letting it fade, and anger breaks the fade.

spore-jar.name: Memory-spore jar
spore-jar.text: A small clay jar with a pale mote inside, cool to the touch. It holds one kept thing.
spore-jar.persona: A small clay jar holding a memory-spore: one kept thing, glowing softly.

moon-token.name: Moon token
moon-token.text: A pale coin, cool on one face and warm on the other. The Hissling gives it to visitors it decides are patient.
moon-token.persona: A pale coin, cool on one face and warm on the other.

topics.speaker: hissling
topics.text: The Hissling says nothing down here is thrown away twice.

topics.speaker: sifter
topics.text: The Sifter says a memory that is never visited fades on its own, and that is tending too.

topics.speaker: hissling
topics.text: The Hissling says the ledger keeps every no as kindly as any yes.
